newsitem.title: POLAND: Polifarb-C shareholder fights bonus issue.
newsitem.headline: Polifarb-C shareholder fights bonus issue.

text.p: A small shareholder of Polish paintmaker Polifarb Cieszyn applied to a court to cancel an earlier shareholder decision to issue 6.375 million bonus shares before a merger with Wroclaw, Cieszyn said.

Cieszyn said in a Wednesday statement that the shareholder, who has 90 of Cieszyn's 19,125,000 shares, said the motion approving the issue was against fair trading practice and was against the company and its shareholders' interest.

Cieszyn currently has 2,978,820 shares fewer than Wroclaw, and a bonus issue of that number of shares under the original merger plan had been designed to make up for the difference, with each firm's shareholders getting half of the new entity.
But Polifarb Cieszyn's shareholders decided that they should get 53.5 percent, increasing the pre-merger bonus issue for Cieszyn shareholders to 6.375 million shares.
Last week Polifarb Wroclaw said that the treasury ministry in turn requested a bonus issue of 10 million shares to shift control of the planned new company in favour of Wroclaw's shareholders.
